A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same one-shot RLVR study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLVR experiments across mathematical benchmarks and ARC, including comparisons across models, training examples, algorithms, and loss ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds format-reward comparisons, in-context learning evaluations, label-noise experiments, prompt ablations, and other original analyses.

M1.justification: The historical-variance selector, example duplication, outcome-reward training, and GRPO/PPO procedures remain unchanged. The loss definitions are retained from v1 Appendix A.1 in v3 Appendix B.1. Format-only rewards and in-context learning are added controls, not replacements for the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The six mathematical benchmarks and ARC-Easy/Challenge remain unchanged. Training scenarios expand modestly: beyond v1's individual incorrect-label tests, v3 examines widespread random-label corruption and a calculation-only version of the multistep training problem (Appendices C.2.4–C.2.5). These extend conditions within the existing mathematical domain.

E2.justification: v3 adds format-reward RLVR to the principal Qwen comparisons, in-context learning with π1 and official Qwen exemplars (Table 16), and a DeepScaleR model trained on 40k examples (Table 12). These introduce substantial evaluated alternatives beyond v1's existing base-model, full-set RLVR, and loss-component comparisons.

E3.justification: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B evaluation changes from an 8k-token limit to reported 8k and 32k settings, with revised decoding settings in v3 Appendix B.5. v3 also evaluates two additional Qwen model configurations and introduces QwQ-32B correctness judging and pass@8 evaluation, distinct from the retained average-pass@1 metrics.

E4.justification: Beyond retained loss and label ablations, v3 adds extensive format-confounding checks, dataset-wide label-noise robustness, prompt-complexity ablation, test-response-length analysis, pass@8 trajectories, and policy-loss dynamics. These test substantial new explanatory questions. The earlier distilled-model training curves in v1 Figures 6 and 12 are removed.

E5.justification: For distilled-model evaluation, v3 Appendix B.5 specifies avg@16 for MATH500, Minerva Math, and OlympiadBench and avg@64 for AIME/AMC, replacing v1's one/eight-sample evaluation defaults. This changes evaluation replication, not documented training-seed replication. Neither version reports confidence intervals or variability across independent training runs.

E6.justification: Headline Qwen results, ARC scores, and existing loss-ablation values are retained, but substantial results are added. For example, v3 reports a format-reward baseline of 65.0% on MATH500 and 28.7% average (Table 8), plus new model, prompting, robustness, and pass@8 results. Distilled-model scores are replaced under revised evaluation conditions, not improved under an unchanged protocol.

T1.justification: The historical-variance definitions and GRPO, advantage, KL, and entropy equations remain mathematically unchanged. v3 Appendix D.3 adds an informal explanation for persistent policy signals after near-saturation, but no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim that one example can match training on thousands, with the same headline scores, remains. v3 narrows effectiveness from 'nearly all' examples to 'many', explicitly claims gains beyond format correction, and qualifies entropy-only improvements as weaker than the format-reward baseline. The conclusion also adds an anti-overfitting interpretation.

C2.justification: v3 substantially revises interpretation by attributing much improvement to format correction while identifying residual advantages over that control. It adds explanations involving prompt complexity and occasional errors sustaining policy signals. Appendix D.1 explicitly states that one-shot RLVR does not save computation and that the selected example need not transfer optimally across models.

D1.justification: Most learning rates, loss weights, hardware information, precision discussion, and resource links are retained or relocated. v3 adds concrete details such as the dataloader's drop_last requirement, the format-reward criterion, and the numerical perturbation procedure for corrupting integer and fractional labels.

R1.justification: The positioning against LIMR and concurrent four-example RLVR remains. v3 adds Absolute Zero to discussion of minimal-supervision RLVR and introduces references supporting LLM judging, in-context learning, label-noise robustness, and exploration. EMPO and TTRL were already cited in v1; their expanded positioning is not a newly added citation.

P1.justification: v3 extensively condenses and rewrites the main experimental narrative, moves related work and extended discussion into appendices, separates detailed training/evaluation settings, and adds a contents section and a more structured analysis appendix. These are substantial organizational changes beyond adding experiments or renumbering sections.

P2.justification: v1's Figure 2 bar chart becomes v3 Table 8, the π13 example moves from Table 2 to appendix Table 21, and the entropy-results display is condensed with full results retained separately. v3 also adds format-baseline curves, numerous analysis tables and plots, and an evaluation-length comparison, while removing the distilled-model training curves.

improvement.justification: v1 did not adequately separate its large accuracy gains from output-format correction. v3's format-reward controls, in-context comparisons, and format-insensitive judging substantially address this central confound while demonstrating remaining advantages (Tables 14–16). Narrower generality claims and explicit computational limitations further improve calibration. Some distilled-model trajectory evidence is lost, and training-run uncertainty remains unreported, but the central empirical claim now has a substantially stronger evidential basis.
